title: People and Teams Product Thesis
problem: CyberAlchemy refers to human participants, owners, reviewers, and collaborators but lacks first-class Person and Team meanings, making it easy to confuse humans with accounts and teams with roles, projects, access groups, or authority.
value_proposition: People and Teams gives CyberAlchemy a stable, privacy-minimizing language for human identity, collective identity, membership, participation roles, and responsibility without turning those facts into permissions or authority.
value_mechanism: Keep Person and Team identities stable, represent membership and role assignment explicitly, attach responsibilities through owned relations, preserve lifecycle history, and reject every inference from participation to authority unless a separate authority record exists.
first_order_principles: a human is not an account or record
a team is not merely its current member set
membership is explicit and historically preserved
role and responsibility do not grant authority
personal data is minimized for the named use
identity, participation, ownership, and authority remain separate
boundaries: no identity verification or human-directory implementation
no employment or organizational hierarchy model
no authentication, authorization, permission, or access-group inference
no private-attribute inference or unnecessary personal-data collection
no Product Capability adoption or runtime claim from ontology validation
hypotheses: stable Person references reduce owner and handoff ambiguity
explicit Team Membership prevents account and role lists from becoming hidden team definitions
separating role, responsibility, and authority reduces accidental permission inflation
privacy-minimizing records make collaboration meaning reusable across CyberAlchemy products
evidence_routes: future Project and Context integration evidence
revision_criteria: the model cannot preserve one Person across relevant CyberAlchemy contexts
Team identity changes silently with membership
a materially smaller model preserves the same boundaries
privacy or authority boundaries fail in real use
owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 People and Teams product owner

revision_history.change: Created the first Person and Team product thesis and explicit non-collapse boundaries.
revision_history.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus People and Teams product owner

challenge_route: Challenge Person or Team canonical meaning through CyberAlchemy v2 definitions governance; challenge product meaning through the People and Teams product owner; challenge a concrete Person, Team, membership, role, or responsibility through its data and meaning owner.
claim_limit: Committed product direction and candidate business meaning only; no Person or Team instance, Product Capability adoption, identity system, authorization system, DomainSpec source, implementation, publication, release, deployment, or external effect.
